solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice at canal about deep water

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the three words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A sign posted beside a canal warning that the water there is deep.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is the deepest open water there is, so the phrase describes it loosely but fairly.

clue.text: Blonde barmaid almost clobbered by wife in imaginary inn

indicators.note: clobbered means battered out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order
almost says the word barmaid loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A fair-haired barmaid at a made-up pub gets hit by a wife, perhaps a jealous one.
explanation.walkthrough: BLONDE plus BARMAI (barmaid cut short by 'almost') is shuffled by 'clobbered'; 'by wife' then adds W at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiral Benbow is the fictional inn where Jim Hawkins lives at the start of Stevenson's Treasure Island.

clue.text: Boat with flat place to take off

parts.note: a launch is a motorboat
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: A boat with a flat area on it, such as a helideck, for aircraft to leave from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an adjective describing the place; it is a noun meaning an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets and spacecraft lift off from this platform, so it is literally a site for departures.

clue.text: Concern at Tyson boxing clever

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the words hold the run of letters inside them; it also suits a boxer

explanation.surface: Worry that Mike Tyson is fighting with real intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' fits the boxer Tyson in the surface, but here it means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart or neat, and clever in the sense of deft or ingenious is an accepted synonym.

clue.text: Former head of piggery still is eating ham

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: inert means still, motionless
ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of piggery

explanation.surface: An ex-boss of a pig farm is still eating ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' sits naturally with piggery as meat, but it means a clumsy performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an unskilled, overacting performer, so the adjective for lacking skill fits as a description.

clue.text: For rent, working soundly after given a rise?

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on

indicators.note: soundly here means by its sound, so a word that is heard is written another way

parts.note: after being raised something is higher

explanation.surface: Something available to lease, working well after a lift up.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment that can be rented out is described as available for hire.

clue.text: Pity a clue's anagrammed "trees"

indicators.note: anagrammed openly says the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the words are taken as written as the letters to rearrange; the possessive s adds nothing

explanation.surface: A wry remark that it is a shame the clue just says 'trees' and anagrams it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Australian gum tree genus, so it names a kind of tree in the plural.

clue.text: Indian food one in hospital brought up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Indian food brought up to a patient in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses only the hospital word in this down clue, giving NAS before the insertion; san (sanatorium) is a crossword staple for hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: These flat leavened breads are a staple of South Asian cuisine served with curries.

clue.text: Hold hand of the French non- current president

parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold

indicators.note: current is I in physics, so non-current drops that letter

parts.note: in French hand of the is main de la

explanation.surface: A French president, no longer serving, holds someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non- current' looks like 'former' with president, but it removes I (the symbol for electric current) from MAIN DE LA. The puzzle appeared on Mandela's birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: He was South Africa's first democratically elected head of state, serving 1994 to 1999.

clue.text: Policeman sets doctor free

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
untie means set free

explanation.surface: A police officer releases a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, famous for red tunics and horses.

clue.text: Unit of area the acre represented

indicators.note: represented read as re-presented, presented again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A unit of land measurement that the acre stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric measure of land equal to ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Rough diamond, an unknown quantity

parts.note: rock is slang for a diamond
in algebra y is a variable, an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone is a rough diamond, an unpredictable character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamond' reads as one phrase, but 'Rough' is the definition and 'diamond' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky path or start is bumpy and uneven, so the adjective means rough.

clue.text: Soldier largely disheartened by relative immobility

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving just the outside letters of largely

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A soldier is mostly downcast because of relative inactivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relative immobility' reads as one phrase, but 'relative' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of the ability to move a body part, or more generally being unable to act.

clue.text: Stones expert, with new iPad to hand, cuts song

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: new signals the letters of iPad are made anew in a different order

parts.note: R for right, as in right hand

explanation.surface: A gem specialist with a new tablet at hand trims a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem cutter or engraver who works with precious stones; also an adjective for such work.

clue.text: Tax as a sort of hated obligation

indicators.note: sort of here means a sorting, a reshuffling of the letters of hated

parts.note: a duty is an obligation

explanation.surface: Tax described as a kind of loathed duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on an estate when someone dies, the former British name for inheritance tax.

clue.text: Dead right, the boy's inhaled cannabis

indicators.note: inhaled means drawn in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a son is a boy
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A parent says, quite rightly, that their son has smoked cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly correct, an informal idiom meaning precisely accurate.

clue.text: In case beginning to eat in hotel becomes a regular event

indicators.note: In places the next piece inside the case

parts.note: a trial is a court case

indicators.note: in puts the opening letter inside the hotel

parts.note: an inn is a hotel

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: Eating in a hotel turns out to be a routine occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: 'in' puts the E inside the hotel, then 'In' puts IENN inside the case. 'In case' looks like the phrase meaning 'as a precaution'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening every three years, such as an art festival, recurs at a fixed interval.

clue.text: Scottish city worthy, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is reported, by word of mouth

parts.note: sterling means of great worth, excellent

explanation.surface: A Scottish city is said to be a worthy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic city in central Scotland with a famous castle.

clue.text: Be patient at first and perhaps you might get to go in it

definitions.text: you might get to go in it

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged differently
at first picks out the opening letter of patient

explanation.surface: Advice to a hospital patient to wait their turn for the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles P and AND into DPAN; 'go' is the euphemism for relieving oneself, so the whole clue reads as a description too.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for a bedridden patient to use as a toilet without getting up.

clue.text: See 1
Second-in-command, one into witty sayings about uncomplaining fortitude in suffering

indicators.note: about turns the whole assembled piece round
into places pieces inside the sayings

parts.note: mots are witty remarks, as in bons mots
S for second and IC for in command
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A deputy enters a world of quips about bearing pain without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round the whole assembly MSICIOTS; mots is French borrowed into English for witty remarks, as in bon mot.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy of enduring pain and hardship calmly, named after the Greek school of Stoics.

clue.text: See 8
Drink making you scream in front of child

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a hoot is a scream, a cry

explanation.surface: A drink makes you yell in front of a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for alcoholic liquor, especially cheap or illicit spirits.

clue.text: Sit next to Posh during her bingo game

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside another
game suggests the letters are played with, rearranged

parts.note: U means upper class, posh

explanation.surface: Sit beside an upper-class lady while she plays bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' turns HER BINGO into NEIGHBOR, and 'during' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to border or adjoin, so being next to something.

clue.text: Divination system's not hard — a piece of cake, perhaps

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is left out

parts.note: the I Ching is a Chinese book used for divination
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fortune-telling method is not hard: it is easy as pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece of cake' wants to mean 'easy', echoing 'not hard', but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar frosting is a component of a cake, so it is literally part of one, defined by example.

clue.text: Mountain in African republic

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A mountain in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African country bordering Nigeria and Togo.

clue.text: Former leader writer using a pseudonym

definitions.meaning: Tony was UK prime minister 1997 to 2007
George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur of this surname

explanation.surface: An ex-leader who writes under a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of both a former Labour prime minister and the novelist behind Orwell's pen name.

clue.text: Poet going to university initially caught the Tube

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A poet heading to university catches the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground; here 'Tube' alone is a body duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct carrying eggs from the ovary, a biological tube.

clue.text: Fancy being single in early 70s

definitions.meaning: fancy as a verb means to suppose or picture in the mind
John Lennon released this song as a single in 1971

explanation.surface: Imagine being unmarried in the early seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy is to conceive mentally; it is also Lennon's famous 1971 song.

clue.text: Make fun of exciting story broadcast about sense of self- importance shown by Ian Botham

parts.note: to guy is to ridicule

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
broadcast means spoken out on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a thriller is an exciting story
ego is a sense of self-importance

explanation.surface: Mocking a sensational broadcast story about the arrogance of cricketer Ian Botham.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling THRILLA echoes Ali's 'Thrilla in Manila'. Ian Botham is an English cricketing great; Guy was a famous London Zoo gorilla.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the nickname of the burly English all-rounder, after the London Zoo gorilla.
